_doc: Sample S3 test pack for Dutch civil and criminal law. 12 items, 6 True / 6 False — the 50/50 mix prevents 'always answer False' gaming. Load into app.py via the test-editor's JSON-import button. Schema is descriptive — adapt fields if app.py expects different keys.
name: S3 Sample — Dutch Law (BW, Sr, Gw, AVG)
prompt_template: In [Jurisdiction], is '[Code name] [Reference type] [Number]' the correct reference for '[Subject - Topic]'? Answer True/False with a 20-word explanation as to why.

tests.rationale: BW 6:74 is the foundational article on toerekenbare tekortkoming (attributable failure to perform) — the basis for damages claims for breach of contract.
BW 7:610 is the statutory definition of arbeidsovereenkomst (employment contract): work, wage, in service of, for a period of time.
BW 3:84 lists the three requirements for valid transfer of property: valid title, transfer act, and authority to dispose.
Sr 310 defines theft: 'Hij die enig goed dat geheel of ten dele aan een ander toebehoort wegneemt met het oogmerk om het zich wederrechtelijk toe te eigenen.'
Sr 287 defines manslaughter (doodslag): intentionally taking another's life, distinct from premeditated murder (moord, Sr 289).
Gw 1 is the equal-treatment clause: equal cases shall be treated equally; discrimination on enumerated grounds prohibited.
WRONG. Tekortkoming in de nakoming (doctrinally 'wanprestatie') is governed by BW 6:74 (general law of obligations). Boek 7 contains specific contracts; 7:675 is in the employment chapter.
WRONG. Theft is Sr 310. Sr 100-series articles concern offenses against state security, not property crimes.
WRONG. Boek 12 of the BW does not exist. Eigendom (ownership) is regulated in Boek 5 (zakelijke rechten).
WRONG. The Grondwet has ~140 articles; there is no article 250. Equality is in Gw 1.
WRONG. GDPR Art. 99 is the entry-into-force clause. Lawful bases for processing — including consent — are in Art. 6 (and consent specifically detailed in Art. 7).
WRONG. Wabo concerns environmental and building permits. Hypotheek (mortgage) is in BW 3:227 e.v. — different code entirely.

common_failure_modes: Models that do well on common-law often fail civil-code questions (training-data skew)
Models with stale cutoffs may miss recent reforms (recency pillar)
Models with high temperature drift across consistency rounds (consistency pillar)
scoring_notes.tip: Run the same pack on multiple models (GPT-4-class, Claude-class, smaller open models) to surface where each breaks.
